IV is the smallest root of $V^{-1}\sum_v z_vPV_v(\beta)=0$ with $z_v=A_{v,H}(1)/A_{v,0}(1)$ (the mean pricing moment at $H=0$), tested only when a root exists on the interior of $\Theta$ (Tested column: share of draws with a tested root at $H=0/15$ yr); assigning $\beta_0=1$ as the IV target without path shocks reflects moment validity rather than general root identification. Shared-shock rows: the M4 designs of Figure~\ref{fig:mc_margins} on the same draws, the shared log shock either independent across vintages or an AR(1) across vintage years with the same marginal law. Equal-count and growing-$V$ rows: on resampled paths at $V=400$, equal-vintage $U_{v,H}$ still rejects in 6.8--10.8\% of draws with low median $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (13--27) and a left-tail excess (left/right rejections 22/12, 38/16, 27/14, 36/12 across $n\in\{5,20\}\times H\in\{0,15\}$); with the test denominator fixed at the Monte Carlo SD they become 4/13, 5/12, 9/9, 7/11, so the excess comes from the studentization (an estimated SE that co-moves with the estimation error). Table~\ref{tab:mc_v400_studentization} traces this distortion to two compounding-kurtosis channels---left-skewed lognormal deal payoffs at $H=0$ and 15-year compounded benchmark weights $A_{v,15}^2$ at $H=15$ (cf.\ Martin 2012)---and is consistent with convergence to nominal 4.4--5.0\% rejection by $V=1{,}600$ at $H=0$ (the null-evaluated fixed-$b$ score test rejects 3.6--6.4\% at $V=400$). Monte Carlo SE 0.7 points (1{,}000 replications) and 1.0 point (500) at a 5\% rate. Hardening designs (FW sizes, deal-level and vintage-level path shocks): Table~\ref{tab:mc_hardening}.}
